personality.buyer: SMBs to mid-market support, service, and CX teams
personality.reasoning: Zoho Desk is an operations-heavy support platform with AI, automation, and omnichannel workflows. The visual language should feel structured and credible, but still modern and interactive—more like a smart service console than a flashy SaaS promo. Since the page emphasizes trust, 100,000+ businesses, and feature depth, the design should use strong hierarchy, clean panels, and layered product-led compositions with clear proof moments.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: Headline is 7 words, so 56px keeps it bold without wrapping awkwardly on desktop while preserving premium impact.

colours.colourReason: Customer support software benefits from a calm, dependable blue foundation that signals control and professionalism. Green is used as the action/accomplishment accent to communicate resolution speed, successful automation, and AI-assisted efficiency.

layout.heroBackground: deep blue gradient with layered product UI shell and floating proof chips
layout.heroReason: The product is SaaS and benefits from a visible interface-led hero. A split layout lets us show the help desk UI, omnichannel context, and AI assistance while keeping the core promise and CTAs highly readable.
layout.featureReason: The content has multiple feature groupings, including AI, integrations, and customization. Spotlight-plus-grid lets us use a hero-like spotlight card for key value props, then supporting cards and tabs for depth.
layout.darkSectionFor: hero and the AI-focused section for contrast and product intelligence

personality.imageryDirection: Use a layered product screenshot composition: Zoho Desk UI mock on the right, with 2-3 floating chips for omnichannel, AI, and automation. If screenshot assets are weak, build a CSS-based interface shell with ticket lists, sentiment badges, and response suggestion panels. Use PNG for product/UI visuals and JPEG only for any large contextual banner art. Keep logos as SVG and feature icons as clean SVG line icons.
personality.designPersonality: Calm, intelligent, and operationally sharp—premium enough for enterprise trust, but tactile enough to feel interactive and product-led. Strong contrast between sections, clean data density, and layered panels create a sense of a modern support command center.

designIntent.audience: Support and operations teams evaluating customer support software
designIntent.primaryUserIntent: Understand whether Zoho Desk can streamline omnichannel ticket handling, improve response speed with AI, and support a free-trial signup

brandDirection.tone: Expert, warm, and efficiency-led; emphasize reliability, faster resolution, and easy adoption without sounding overly technical
brandDirection.visualStyle: Content-first, utility-focused layout with a strong dark hero, clean white feature sections, and flat bordered cards; minimal decoration, clear scanning hierarchy

sectionPurpose.purpose: Create immediate relevance, establish product value, and push the primary conversion action through a prominent free-trial CTA
Reinforce credibility early with award and customer-count proof so users feel safe moving deeper
Explain the core value proposition of Zoho Desk through feature-led benefit scanning
Differentiate the product through AI capability and decision-support value
Reduce adoption friction by showing fit with the user's existing tools and ecosystem
Address configurability concerns and show adaptability to business workflows
Convert intent into action with a product-plan style purchase block and a strong CTA
Add final credibility and social reassurance before or after pricing interaction

componentNeeds.variantHint: Content-first hero with strong brand-colour background, headline, subheadline, supporting line, dual CTAs, and compact value bullets
componentNeeds.notes: Because no hero media is provided, prefer a centered or text-dominant layout. Keep the primary CTA visually dominant. Secondary CTA should be less prominent but still visible. Use the long headline sizing rule for 16+ words.

componentNeeds.variantHint: Horizontal proof strip with award badge and customer-count stat
componentNeeds.notes: Use a light grey background to separate from the hero. Keep this section concise and immediately readable.

componentNeeds.variantHint: 4-card grid with descriptive titles and short supporting copy
componentNeeds.notes: Use bordered white cards with clear internal spacing. Prioritize scanning and avoid visual clutter.
Visually differentiate this section subtly through label or section rhythm, but keep the same card system for consistency.

componentNeeds.variantHint: Compact multi-item integration grid or grouped list tiles
componentNeeds.notes: Since no logos are supplied, present integrations as structured grouped items. Keep emphasis on compatibility and ecosystem fit.
Make this feel operational and practical, not decorative. Use clear labels for layouts, blueprints, extensions, and help center.

componentNeeds.variantHint: Centered pricing/product card with included-features checklist and one primary CTA
componentNeeds.notes: Since no numeric price is available, present as a product plan inclusion card rather than a price comparison block. Keep CTA strong and conversion-focused.

componentNeeds.variantHint: Quote cards with author identity and support-role framing
componentNeeds.notes: Only use the supplied testimonials. If a testimonial is partial, preserve it carefully or treat it as incomplete content rather than expanding it.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a dark, trust-forward hero with white text, compact supporting bullets, and side-by-side CTAs; because there is no product image, prioritize a text-centric single-panel composition with strong above-fold hierarchy
layoutStrategy.features: Arrange feature sections as modular white cards in 2-column on desktop and 1-column on mobile, with consistent headings, short descriptions, and predictable spacing for easy scanning
layoutStrategy.proof: Place trust signals immediately after the hero in a light grey strip to front-load credibility before feature exploration
layoutStrategy.pricing: Use a centered elevated product cart layout with a checklist of included capabilities and a full-width CTA; avoid introducing unsupported pricing values
layoutStrategy.form: No standalone lead form is provided, so let CTA buttons carry conversion; if a form appears later in the funnel, it should be a compact, low-friction capture module

designIntent.tokenProfileHint: Default to Techjockey's professional marketplace system with a trust-authority leaning hero, dark primary palette, accent CTA contrast, Inter body text, and a clean utility-card component set; keep motion subtle and spacing disciplined
designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Design a single-product landing page for Zoho Desk that opens with a strong, content-first hero focused on free-trial conversion, immediately followed by trust proof, then a linear sequence of modular feature grids covering core value, AI differentiation, integrations, and customization. End with a product-cart style pricing/inclusion block and supported testimonials. The overall feel should be credible, efficient, and easy to scan, using consistent bordered cards, generous section spacing, and minimal decorative complexity.

figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Default Techjockey marketplace system with product-category-specific styling for customer support software; use Plus Jakarta Sans heading and Inter body, white/light-grey content sections, blue-primary CTA treatment, and utility-card components throughout.

sections.notes: Use a single centered hero because no primary media is provided. Include top strip CTA as a compact utility link above the main headline. Keep two CTAs side by side with primary visually dominant. Supporting line should be rendered as a compact trust/value line under CTAs. Background must use primary brand colour treatment per memory, with light text.

Place immediately below hero. Show Award badge and Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally with divider-separated horizontal items. Keep to light grey background. Do not add extra trust claims beyond provided content and memory alignment.

Use section headline + description followed by a 4-card feature grid. White cards with 1px border and 12px radius. No icons were provided, so use colored SVG icon slots from system rather than placeholders. Maintain clean scanning.

Second feature section with the same grid system but different content theme. Preserve section header hierarchy and card consistency. Use system iconography and keep descriptions concise inside cards.
Render as a compact multi-card or chip-card grid based on five items. Keep tool names in a strong title line and the ecosystem examples in the body line. Maintain equal card heights where possible.

Use the same section wrapper and feature-card system for consistency. Keep this section visually lighter than the previous AI section to avoid repetition fatigue; vary card icon color only, not structure.

Use centered pricing card layout even though no prices are supplied. Since original price, discount, and EMI are missing, omit price row but still preserve plan card structure, included-features checklist, and primary CTA. Use the exact product name and checklist items. Keep it as a conversion block on a light grey background, following the cart pattern.

Only two testimonials are available, so use a two-card desktop grid instead of forcing three columns. Apply testimonial card styling with left accent border and star row. If second testimonial content is incomplete, keep the card structure and show only the provided text without inventing missing author details.

Use a minimal closing CTA band to surface Get Your Free Trial and Get Started again without creating a separate form section. Keep it structurally simple, consistent with the page's form-led intent, but do not invent input fields because none are provided.

Stack all hero content vertically. Primary CTA should be full width, secondary CTA full width below it. Keep the supporting line concise and wrap naturally. Preserve the top strip CTA as a small text action above headline if space allows.
Collapse trust bar into a compact stacked cluster if needed while keeping award badge and customer count visible. Avoid truncation of 100,000+ value.
Convert 4-card grid to single-column cards with consistent spacing and card heights. Keep titles short and readable. Maintain the same card component family as desktop.
Single-column cards on mobile. Keep content density comfortable and avoid squeezing all copy into one viewport. Use the same system card paddings and borders.

Because this section has five items, use stacked compact cards or two-up chip rows only if space permits. Favor readability over dense compression. Preserve the exact integration categories and examples.
Maintain the same section structure as prior feature blocks. Keep each card self-contained and easy to scan with generous internal padding.
Use a full-width card with no shadow emphasis beyond the system default. Since no pricing values are present, keep the layout but omit price-only nodes. The checklist and CTA remain mandatory.
Render testimonials as vertically stacked cards. Preserve quote styling and author hierarchy. If the second testimonial is incomplete, keep it visually consistent but only use supplied text.
Keep the closing conversion band simple and full width. Stack primary and secondary CTA buttons. Do not introduce a form because no form content is provided.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and Inter for body across the page.
Keep the hero dark/primary-tinted with light text per brand memory; do not use a white hero.
Do not invent a pricing amount; maintain the pricing card structure with included-features checklist and CTA only.
Reuse one feature-card component family for all product sections and swap content only.
Treat testimonials as a two-item set on desktop because only two entries are provided.
Keep all sections deterministic with consistent container width, section padding, and border-led utility styling.
No form section is built because the input payload contains an empty form object with no fields.

heroStrategy.designNote: Use a premium operational-dashboard hero: deep blue mesh-gradient background, left-aligned copy, and a layered product UI on the right showing ticket queues, AI suggestions, and omnichannel context. Keep the composition structured and trust-heavy, with floating proof chips over the media panel and a subtle gradient overlay for contrast. Avoid stock photography; prioritize product-led visuals with clean, card-based depth and a smart service-console feel.

blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk Price Plan Includes: | Deliver Exceptional Customer Support
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Desk to streamline ticket management, automate workflows, enable omnichannel support, and deliver smarter customer service with AI-powered assistance.

sections.backgroundTreatment: deep blue gradient with subtle grid texture, floating proof chips, and a layered UI shell
sections.designNote: Create a dynamic above-the-fold split hero with the headline, subheadline, supporting line, and two pill CTAs on the left. On the right, show a product UI mock with ticket queue, omnichannel badges, and an AI suggestion panel. Add a compact top strip CTA for 'Talk to Expert' and keep the premium trust tone strong and readable.

Use a compact horizontal trust strip with a badge for 'Award' and a prominent proof statement showing 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally'. Keep it lightweight, utility-driven, and immediately adjacent to the hero to reinforce credibility.

Build this as a stacked set of alternating product blocks with strong section contrast. For 'Why Choose Zoho Desk?' use a spotlight panel with a 2x2 feature grid. For 'Make Smarter Support Decisions with Zia AI' switch to a darker, more intelligent section with a feature spotlight and AI response preview. For integrations and customization, use modular card grids with concise labels and optional preview shells. This section should feel product-led and layered, with clear hierarchy and card boundaries.

The source input disables this section, so omit it from the page or reserve it as a hidden/conditional block if needed by the CMS. If surfaced later, present it as a compact icon-list or counter grid with strong utility messaging.

Present a centered highlighted pricing/product cart card titled 'Zoho Desk' with the included feature list as check rows. Since pricing values are absent, keep the emphasis on value inclusion and a strong 'Get Started' CTA rather than numeric discounting. Use a crisp bordered card with subtle elevation and clear spacing.

Use a testimonial slider with prominent quote cards. Keep the first quote fully visible and include author, role, and company metadata. Since only two testimonials are provided, use a carousel-style treatment with one featured card and a supporting secondary card to preserve visual balance.

Use a centered floating lead-capture card with clear spacing and high-contrast form controls. If the form fields remain empty, present this as a conversion-ready placeholder block with the primary CTA emphasized. Keep the surface clean, bordered, and calm to maintain trust and reduce friction.
Since no news items are provided, either omit this section or convert it into a minimal brand/partner logo strip if the CMS requires a closing trust block. Keep it understated and non-distracting.
